claim: R8 asks for D_1 on all local operators; what is computed is only the two-body log kernel (4 lc^natural). The composite two-body kernel C^(2)_Delta and the one-body C^(1)_Delta (A_V, lambda, c) are computed by neither engine, so every D_1 number reported for gauge-invariant families (two_site.json D1_eigenvalues_units, kernels.json D1 'spectrum_at_theta=-1/3_under_P7', P5 eig(D_1) = -8 E_H u) is conditional on the untested prediction P7. On the bilinears the engines take the composite triangle -2u {S^(1)(Delta),O} from Prop c9-triangle; Remark c9-twoeval states that 'this agreement determines both coefficients 8 in the value of the composite triangle', i.e. that input was fixed by consistency, not evaluated. D_1 on the bilinears is therefore an input to R8, not a check of it.
evidence: engine_a/kernels.json D1.two_body: 'C^(2)_Delta ... NOT computed by engine A'; engine_b/NOTES.md 'the composite parts ... are not computed by route B'; compare.json open_issues[0]; manuscript ch09 Rem rem:c9-twoeval last sentence. The referee confirms 4 lc^natural (R7, R9, R10) but has no independent value for C_Delta.
fix: Evaluate C^(2)_Delta (composite cycles through a pair, composite kernel 2(P* v. P* (x) 1)K_0 of Def c9-composite) directly, first for (A_perp, A_perp) without derivatives (this independently reproduces or refutes Prop c9-triangle), then for the twist-two pairs (d^a Z, d^b Z) and (A_n, Z), to test P7. Until then label every D_1 eigenvalue 'conditional on P7, theta = -1/3' and quote spectra as 2 eig lc^natural = gamma.
two_component: D_1 = 4 lc^natural - {F'_Delta,-} + C_Delta; on (A_ij, A_kl) only the term u[8 A_kl A_ij - 2 eps_ijkl A^mn A_mn] (= 4 x two-site log kernel) is computed.

claim: Lemma lem:tl-colour labels the outputs opposite to Def def:tl-cycle and to both engines. With Y_1 at the vertex nearest X_a (the numbering of Def tl-cycle), the chain gives the colour element sum t_gamma (x) ad_{Y_k}...ad_{Y_1} t^gamma, and the planar replacement is Y_1...Y_k. The Lemma writes w = ad_{Y_1}...ad_{Y_r} and 'replaced by Y_r...Y_1' without saying which Y is nearest X_a. Combining the Lemma's order with the Def tl-cycle numbering swaps the swap and identity terms of the planar density: u[2P - K] becomes u[2 - K], which gives lc^natural = 0 on every su(2) state and contradicts the Heisenberg spectrum.
evidence: Referee derivation of the colour contraction along the chain (ref_core.py docstring) and t_colour.py (explicit gl(N) matrices): the leading term is +N tr(M1 Y_1 Y_2) with Y_1 nearest X_a. The engines use this reading (kernels.json meta 'tr(... Y_1 ... Y_r ...)'), and the su(2) and twist-two spectra (R7, R9) confirm it.
fix: In Lemma lem:tl-colour (i) state 'Y_r adjacent to X_a, Y_1 adjacent to X_b' or rewrite (i)-(iii) with w = ad_{Y_r}...ad_{Y_1} (Y_1 nearest X_a) and 'replaced by Y_1...Y_r'.

claim: In two_site.json the 'D1_eigenvalues_units' strings omit u (already compare F-3). They also append '- (1/3+theta) v.', which is the classical dilatation operator and not a number, so the strings mix an operator with eigenvalues. The engine A notes give 'one-body parts in units' A_V -22/3, lambda -47/3, c -8/3; these leave out the nonlocal C^(1)_Delta, and only the sum C^(1)+C^(2) is local.
evidence: engine_b/two_site.json twist_two['8'].D1_eigenvalues_units = ['-3044/35 - (1/3+theta) v.', ...]; engine_a/kernels.json D1.one_body_units. Arithmetic checked: -4 n_F - {F'_Delta,-} gives -8+2/3 = -22/3, -16+1/3 = -47/3, -4+4/3 = -8/3, and with Pi_Delta|perp the A_perp value -8 + (5/3 - theta) v.
fix: Report eigenvalues as numbers times u (conditional on P7, N1) and keep the classical part separate. Label the A_V, lambda, c one-body numbers 'without C^(1)_Delta (nonlocal)'.
